{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-in-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"61d8afbc04424bc2f5fbd1bff1bea2b33d9d54ca4e7470e39467fd35779da9f0","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:5","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","source_liveness_sha256":"4d2b75b9a10fb774f53fb2d906a3a7a7f75f5e9387f8b4ddcd423e9b7828d59b"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Getting the license: skills exam scoring, financial liability, license requirements, probationary rules and public safety laws","heading":"C — Skills exam scoring and automatic failures, financial liability for minors, license age and practice requirements, license validity, probationary passenger and hour limits, school-related suspension, CDL basics, mail delivery, seat belts and phones","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Skills exam scoring and automatic failures, financial liability for minors, license age and practice requirements, license validity, probationary passenger and hour limits, school-related suspension, CDL basics, mail delivery, seat belts and phones
Knowledge domain: what turns a learner's permit into an Indiana driver's license — how the driving skills exam is scored and failed, who must accept financial liability for a minor, the age, holding-period and practice-log rules, how long licenses last, the probationary limits on passengers, hours and phones, and the seat belt and texting laws every driver must follow.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Skills exam errors that can lower your score or fail you include not using the defroster or wipers when needed, not keeping both hands on the wheel, picking the wrong gear and not signaling. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Driving too slowly, stopping when there is no need, rolling past a crosswalk, stop line or stop sign, turning into or out of the wrong lane and skipping the blind-spot check also count against you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Disobeying a yield, stop, school zone or no-turn-on-red sign, or disobeying a traffic signal, fails the skills exam automatically. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Backing over a curb, striking a parked vehicle, not following instructions or not using a seat belt is an automatic failure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Speeding, driving too fast for the conditions, not reacting to hazardous conditions and turning into or using the wrong lane are automatic failures. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
Passing in a no-passing zone or otherwise going over a solid yellow line, drifting left of the street center and straddling marked lanes each fail the exam automatically. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
Getting too close to pedestrians or bicycles, not pulling over and stopping for emergency vehicles or school buses, causing a crash, failing to yield and breaking railroad crossing laws are automatic failures. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
After failing a driving skills exam you must wait seven days before you may retake it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
A permit holder who fails the skills exam a third time must wait two months from that last failure before testing again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
A permit or probationary license applicant under 18 needs an adult to appear at a BMV branch and sign a sworn or affirmed financial liability statement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
The financial liability signer is chosen in a legal order: the custodial parent or that parent's designee, then the noncustodial parent or designee, then the custodial guardian, then any other willing adult. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
The adult who signs becomes jointly and severally responsible with the minor for damage caused by driving and must show valid identification from the BMV identity document list. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
The signer can withdraw at any time with State Form 55834, and that written request cancels the minor's permit or license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A minor under the care and supervision of the Department of Child Services needs no adult signature but must show a motor vehicle insurance policy meeting Indiana's minimum liability standards. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A driver's license issued to someone under 21 is a probationary license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
A CDL applicant must be at least 18, and a CDL with a school bus endorsement requires age 21. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
To get a license you must meet the age rule, hold a valid Indiana permit for the required time unless you hold an unexpired license from another jurisdiction, prove identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency, and pass vision, knowledge and skills exams. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
The knowledge exam must be completed before the skills exam, which is taken with a BMV examiner or an approved driver training school. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A03
The minimum license age is 16 for someone who completed a BMV licensed driver education program and 16 years and 270 days for someone who did not. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A03
A license applicant must have held a valid Indiana learner's permit for at least 180 days, unless the applicant is 18 or older with a documented disability and has finished rehabilitation training with a BMV-recognized specialist. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
An applicant aged 18 or older must log at least 50 hours of supervised practice with a validly licensed driver aged 25 or more or a licensed spouse aged 21 or more. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A03
At least 10 of the 50 practice hours must be driven at night unless the permit carries daytime-only restriction G, and even then the full 50 hours are required. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A03
The practice hours are proven with State Form 54706, Log of Supervised Driving Practice, submitted when applying; several logs may be used, and a parent or legal guardian signs if the applicant is under 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A03
A disabled applicant who completed rehabilitation training with a BMV-recognized specialist may apply while holding a valid permit, after passing a skills exam with a BMV examiner. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A03
A disabled applicant aged 16 or 17 must still hold the permit for at least 180 days and submit a practice log, while one aged 18 or older has no holding period and no log. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A03
A driver's license lasts six years for drivers under 75, three years for ages 75 through 84 and two years from age 85. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
An applicant under 18 seeking a probationary license must complete at least 50 hours of supervised driving practice. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A04
Supervisors for under-18 practice can be a licensed relative by blood, marriage or legal status aged at least 25, a licensed spouse aged at least 21, a licensed driver training school instructor working for a school, or a BMV-recognized driver rehabilitation specialist. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A04
A license obtained before age 21 stays probationary until 21, expires at 21 years and 30 days, and cannot be renewed before 21 years and one day. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A04
During the first 180 days a probationary driver may carry no passengers unless the front passenger seat holds a licensed driver aged 25 or more, a licensed spouse aged 21 or more, or a driver training school instructor licensee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A04
In those first 180 days the probationary driver may still carry their own child, stepchild, sibling, step or half sibling, or spouse without another adult present. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A04
A probationary driver may not drive between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. during the first 180 days. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A04
After 180 days, a probationary driver under 18 may not drive after 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, before 5 a.m. Monday through Friday, or between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A04
Driving during restricted hours is allowed when going to, taking part in or returning from lawful work, a school-sanctioned activity or a religious event, or when riding with a licensed driver aged 25 or more or a licensed spouse aged 21 or more. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A04
Indiana law bars every driver, probationary holders included, from driving while using any telecommunications device such as a phone, PDA, pager or texting device, except to make a 911 emergency call. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A04
The BMV must suspend a juvenile's driving privileges when a school administrator or principal reports an expulsion, an exclusion, or a second or later suspension within one school year. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A05
Being found a habitual truant or withdrawing from school also leads to the same required suspension of a juvenile's driving privileges. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A05
Renewing a probationary license after turning 21 produces an unrestricted license without the probationary limits. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A05
A commercial learner's permit or CDL requires age 18, and drivers under 21 may drive a commercial vehicle only within Indiana and cannot get school bus endorsements. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A05
A new, renewed, amended or replacement credential is mailed from a secure central location within 14 calendar days, only to the mailing address on file, and it is not forwarded. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A05
Every occupant of a moving vehicle must wear the seat belt when the vehicle has manufacturer-installed belts as standard equipment. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A05
Typing, sending or reading a text or email on a device while driving is illegal unless the device is used hands-free or by voice, or to make a 911 emergency call. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0016]

Misconceptions: a failed skills exam cannot be retaken the next day like the knowledge exam; withdrawing financial liability cancels the minor's permit or license rather than just removing the signer; a daytime-only permit removes the night-hour requirement but not the full practice-hour total; probationary status lasts until twenty-one, not eighteen.
Mnemonics: seven days after a fail, two months after the third; in the first hundred eighty days nobody rides along unless a qualified adult sits up front, family excepted; ten p.m. to five a.m. is off limits in that same opening period.
Glossary: probationary license means the license held by drivers under twenty-one; financial liability means the adult's sworn promise to share responsibility for a minor's driving damage; restriction G means daytime-only driving; jointly and severally means each signer can be held responsible for the full damage; unrestricted license means the license received when renewing after twenty-one.
Dynamic facts: state form numbers, mail delivery times and the BMV website and kiosk options can change; confirm them on IN.gov/BMV.
